findings_rechecked.verification: Diffed packages/runtime/lib/intake.mjs 887ae5ac..3f686871: RECOVERY_BATCH now bounds ACTIONS handled (handled += 1 only on a usable meta), a separate RECOVERY_OPEN_BUDGET = RECOVERY_BATCH * 3 bounds opens, and an unusable read (null/corrupt/id-less) is counted and logged once per sweep instead of silently consuming a slot. Re-ran the two new cells independently: 'p966.budget: sidecars the belt cannot USE never spend the ten slots it acts with' (12 junk entries ahead of one crashed intake -> crashed.reads===1, deferred===1) and 'p966.budget: ...and the READ bound survives' (60 junk entries -> exactly 30 opened, crashed.reads===0, TTL reaper is the stated backstop) both pass, 3 runs. sweepSpoolTtl's regex was also widened from the strict 36-hex-uuid form to /^intake-.+\.(?:bin|json)$/i so a non-uuid junk sidecar is now reapable; 'p966.reap' cell passes.

Diffed intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs: new ownSpool(t) helper mkdtemps a private CLARA_SPOOL_DIR per cell and restores the previous value in t.after; applied to every filesystem-touching cell (p966.race, p966.expire, p966.resume, both p966.listing cells, p966.reap, p966.giveup). Re-ran the exact reproduction from the review: CLARA_INTAKE_SIDECAR_QUIET_MS=1 node --test tests/intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs no longer reds p966.expire (was 'not ok 7... 2 !== 1' on 887ae5ac); with the fix it fails ONLY the two p966.quiet cells, whose subject is the guard itself.

Diffed spool.mjs: RENAME_RETRY_MS default changed from 2000 to 250 (Math.max(0, Number(process.env.CLARA_SPOOL_RENAME_RETRY_MS || 250))). New cell p966.giveup holds a read handle on the meta file, writes over it, and asserts (win32) the original EPERM surfaces, elapsed < 1000ms, and no .tmp residue remains. Re-ran it directly 3 times: elapsed 266-278ms every run, well under the assertion and consistent with a ~250ms deadline. CLARA_SPOOL_RENAME_RETRY_MS=0 still reds only p966.race (13/14), confirming the retry is not vacuous at the new default.

Adversarial review itself said 'None required' for this note (behaviour change is intentional and covered by the ticket's own criterion). Fix round additionally added a sentence to packages/runtime/README.md's Order paragraph stating out loud that a sweep which cannot record its own beat now skips this belt too. Confirmed present in the README diff 887ae5ac..3f686871. No code or test change was needed or made.

Adversarial review explicitly scoped this to the orchestrator's pre-release check of hosted alerts/saved searches matching the old 'chat clarify belt error' string; 'No code change needed.' Fix round's own report confirms it made no change here. Nothing to re-verify in the lane's code or tests; this is a release-time check, not a lane defect.

packages/runtime/README.md's #852 section previously overstated that a chatClarify counter key is 'positive evidence that the belt ran'; the belt returns the same zeroed bag with no statement when resumeHook is absent or delivery columns aren't present. Diff confirms the sentence now reads 'the belt was REACHED and did not throw -- not that it did any work' and names both dormant cases. The reviewer's alternative (a new sweep cell exercising a live resting row) was correctly not taken -- that is coverage, not the defect, and control-chat-clarify.test.mjs already covers the belt directly.

Both the adversarial review ('Consistent with the ticket's scope... recorded rather than charged. None for this ticket.') and the fix round ('recorded by the reviewer as out of #966's scope and stays a follow-up') treat this as out-of-scope for the ticket. Confirmed listIntakeMetas/listIntakeMetaEntries were the only listing changed; listTaskMetas() is untouched by this diff (git diff 887ae5ac..3f686871 -- packages/runtime/lib/spool.mjs shows no change to listTaskMetas), matching the record that it was deliberately left alone.

The exact contention duration a real stuck AV/indexer handle holds on a production host was not independently measured here; the 250ms default is accepted on the same reasoning the fix round gave (a reader handle is microseconds; 250ms is already 1000x that), not on a fresh measurement of production contention.
